key_insight: Higher Ni-based powder content and coating densification drive formation of harder Al–Ni intermetallics, improving wear resistance, with the best performance at 50 wt% Ni/Al–Al + 50 wt% Al and 900 μm thickness.
engineering_relevance: The study links APS feedstock design and coating thickness directly to durability, offering a practical route to optimize protective coatings for wear-critical components.
method: APS deposited Al–Ni coatings on AISI 304 stainless steel using two powder-mixture systems and varied Ni content (10–50 wt%) and thickness (300–900 μm).
Characterized phase/microstructure with XRD and SEM, then measured hardness and pin-on-disc wear.
Built a 3D FE wear model with modified Archard law and adaptive remeshing to predict wear evolution.
evidence_signal: XRD showed β-NiAl in all coatings and γ′-Ni3Al only at the highest Ni content; hardness rose from 74 to 167 HV and from 81 to 178 HV, while the best coating reduced wear loss to 11.2 mg and FE wear volume to 0.153 mm³.
watch_item: The thickness–wear trend differed between the two powder systems, so the optimal design is feedstock-specific and should be validated for the target service condition.
paper_title: Structure property and wear correlations in Al–Ni intermetallic coatings produced by atmospheric plasma spraying
